purpose: Teach: 吹雪/かぜ/つゆ/ぬき/エスカレーター/キッズ/段差/中高

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、吹雪、絶対、お父さん、絶対、外で、絶対、苦労したぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Remember when you were younger? When your father had to struggle through those terrible blizzards outside…
lines.style: Gentle, nostalgic opening. Soft emphasis on the memory itself, not the hardship. Slow, deliberate pace. Voice settles like he's sitting with the warmth of the past. Slight rise at the question mark, searching her face.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、若い頃、絶対、かぜ、絶対、ひくと、絶対、よく、絶対、寝込んだわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh yes. I remember how you'd catch cold so easily back then, and you'd be bedridden for days…
lines.style: Warm, affectionate recall. Lilting cadence on the memory. A small smile in her voice — not mocking, just the tenderness of having nursed him. Trailing softly at the end, reaching for his acknowledgment.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんの、絶対、お料理の、絶対、つゆ、絶対、お父さん、絶対、大好きだったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: And I remember your broths back then. The way your father loved them…
lines.style: Wistful, almost reverent. Slow, deliberate. Lingers on the word for broth — tasting the memory. Quiet certainty underneath, like he can still taste it. Eyes slightly distant.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、ご飯、絶対、ぬき、絶対、で、絶対、お酒、絶対、よく、絶対、飲んだわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh, I remember that. You'd skip the rice and just drink sake every evening…
lines.style: Playful, knowing tease with an edge. Light, almost teasing rhythm. Warmth underneath the ribbing — she's not accusing, she's reminding him. A bit of mischief in her voice, the comfort of an old joke.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、デパートに、絶対、エスカレーター、絶対、初めて、絶対、できた時、絶対、驚いたぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Do you remember when the escalator was first installed at the department store? How amazed you were…
lines.style: Nostalgic, slightly amazed himself at the memory. Slow, almost childlike wonder on the word 'escalator.' Gentle pause before he speaks to her — checking if she remembers too. Voice carries both the marvel of then and the tenderness of now.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんが、絶対、キッズ、絶対、向けの、絶対、お洋服、絶対、孫に、絶対、買ってあげたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, and I remember how you'd buy those children's clothes for our grandchildren…
lines.style: Warm, genuinely tender recall. Gentle, unhurried. Voice brightens slightly — the memory of her generosity. Soft, affectionate on 'grandchildren.' Reaching toward him gently at the end, seeking the shared memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔、本気で、絶対、家の、絶対、段差、絶対、お父さん、絶対、低くしたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Do you remember when I lowered the step at home so your father could manage it…
lines.style: Quiet pride mixed with nostalgia. Matter-of-fact delivery — he did what needed doing. But underneath, there's deep care. Measured pace. The word 'lowered' carries the weight of how much he cared for his own father.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、孫が、絶対、中高、絶対、生になった時、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、喜んだわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: I remember how happy you were when our grandchild started junior high school…
lines.style: Tender, deeply affectionate. Warm, even voice. Slight rise in tone on 'happy' — the genuine joy she felt. Close and intimate, like she's sharing something precious. Reaches across to him, voice wrapping around the memory.
